image_prompt: Peter Pan, a delicate boy appearing approximately twelve years old with an ethereal, androgynous beauty that defies ordinary childhood. His frame is slender and graceful, with an otherworldly poise suggesting exposure to fairy ceremonies. He possesses fine, sharp features with large, luminous eyes that shift between mischievous delight and mercurial melancholy. His hair is tousled and dark, with an almost supernatural gleam. He wears a simple tunic in soft sage or moss green with leaf-like embroidery, accented with delicate golden threads that catch lamplight. His clothing has an antiquated, almost timeless quality—part Edwardian child's wear, part fairy enchantment. One arm reaches toward his shadow, which appears as a separate, slightly corporeal form beside him, rendered in deeper tones. His expression conveys simultaneous vanity and vulnerability, with an irresistible charm in his features. His skin has a faint luminescence as though touched by moonlight and magic. Every detail suggests both youthful innocence and ageless otherworldliness—a boy caught between worlds, neither wholly mortal nor entirely fey.
